entries.title: Home Mixer interaction weights: likes, clicks, sharing and dwell
entries.summary: The later Home Mixer defaults change seven coefficients. This supersedes the old coefficient table for this service at the reviewed revision, not the historical record or every live request.
details: Favorite 0.66 -> 0.708; Click 0.3 -> 0.274; VideoOpen 0.02 -> 0; Share 2 -> 2.118; ContDwellTime 0.006 -> 0.0075; ContClickDwellTime 0.4 -> 0.385; NotInterested -52.272 -> -53.07. The change is in commit 021afa44cb5c5b10afa773cb52c0f5087603d478.
Reply remains 5, Retweet remains 1, ShareViaCopyLink remains 20 and ShareViaDm remains 5. Share and Retweet are separate predictions.

VM Ranker has its own unchanged defaults: Favorite 0.5, Click 0.3, VideoOpen 0.07, Share 2, ContDwellTime 0.004, ContClickDwellTime 0.4, NotInterested -47.52. Never label the Home Mixer numbers as universal VM Ranker values.

Holding a 5-second prediction fixed, the Home Mixer continuous-dwell term goes from 5*0.006=0.03 to 5*0.0075=0.0375. That term increases 25%; the final score and impressions do not thereby increase 25%.

The later FavoriteWeight of 0.708 disproves a present-tense claim that 0.66 is the highest value in all X history. The earlier maximum among the examined October snapshots stays 0.66; this review does not establish an all-time maximum across every version or experiment.
entries.practical_meaning: Make the promise of the opening worth reading through. Do not optimize a publishing calendar or predict impressions from one coefficient.
limits: These are public defaults for named services, not a dump of the effective feature switches for every request. Predictions, other score terms, filtering and competition still matter.
The earlier October 0.004 -> 0.006 change remains a historical fact; do not rewrite Q03 as if the old 50% comparison never occurred.

The public CLICK_DWELL_TIME training output is a binary probability; the full adapter to the Home Mixer field and its raw-label units remain unverified. The new 0.385 coefficient does not resolve Q05 and cannot be described as points per second.

evidence.label: Home Mixer VM request and fallback

entries.title: Home excursion predictions: time after opening a video or profile
entries.summary: Home Mixer now enables existing excursion score support by default and selects an aggregation type with those heads.
details: PhoenixAggregationType changes from DENSE_WITH_LONG_DWELL to DENSE_WITH_LONG_DWELL_HOME_EXCURSION; EnableHomeExcursionScores changes false -> true.
The existing scorer can request home_video_continuation_secs and home_profile_visit_secs. These fields were not first invented in this interval.
Public local and VM video-continuation/profile-visit coefficients remain zero. A prediction being requested is different from a nonzero direct score contribution.
entries.practical_meaning: Judge a video or profile visit by whether the destination is useful. This change alone supplies no new guaranteed video or profile bonus.
limits: An enabled prediction path does not establish the active model or scoring settings for all traffic.

entries.title: Training configuration: time gaps, excursion history and view loss
entries.summary: The named home_direct_packed training configuration changes. Its view-loss reduction is not a halving of the ranking reward for reading.
details: view_loss_weight changes 1 -> 0.5 for binary RECAP_DWELLED, RECAP_NOT_DWELLED and VIDEO_QUALITY_VIEW losses, not the continuous-dwell ranking coefficient.

The config adds continuation loss 0.013 and profile-visit loss 0.0035, enables time-gap features (learning-rate scale 4) and excursion history. The gaps describe request/impression history, not a recommended interval between creator posts.
The base continuous and immersive CREAD loss weights remain 0.1. CREAD predicts continuous actions; it is not a new explicit Article-completion reward.

Other changes include packed candidate length [32,128] -> [128], history mean 510 -> 414, embedding decay 2.8e-4 -> 5.6e-4, stochastic rounding and optimizer settings. The named GB300 configuration does not inherit every home_direct_packed override.
Ordinary DWELL_TIME label validation accepts 0 through 86400 seconds; this check does not establish excursion-label limits or a full-day reading reward.
entries.practical_meaning: Keep writing for actual reader interest. These training settings cannot tell a creator to wait a fixed number of hours or target a specific word count.
limits: A checked-in configuration does not prove deployment to every reader. Model-training loss weights and ranking coefficients belong to different stages.

entries.title: Video Carousel click model, extra score terms and filters
entries.summary: The separate Video Carousel gains an optional click model and filtering support; its overall switch and the click-model switch remain false in public defaults.
details: When a CTR model is available the helper returns its score from the video-open prediction and embedding. The linear model uses an intercept, a clipped-logit open term and 1024 embedding weights; its returned score is a logit, not directly a probability.
The fallback is a*P(open) + b*immersiveVQV + c*P(open)*immersiveDwell + d*weightedScore + e*P(open)*continuationSecs. New d and e defaults are zero.

EnableVideoCarousel=false, EnableVideoCarouselCtrModel=false, EnableVideoCarouselSeenFilter=false; high-risk filtering changes false -> true and medium-risk filtering defaults false. The high-risk filter also rejects candidates with missing brand-safety verdicts.
The optional seen hydrator reads up to 2000 IDs over three days and checks both original and candidate IDs. Its operation is gated by Carousel and seen-filter switches.
Carousel VideoOpenWeight remains 1.0; the ordinary Home Mixer VideoOpenWeight=0 does not replace it. The extra-candidate setting remains 30, now parameterized.
entries.practical_meaning: Use video where movement or demonstration improves the explanation. There is no basis here to promise a platform-wide video boost.
limits: Separate Carousel and ordinary Home paths, model availability and feature switches. Q12 remains unresolved for actual rollout and measured effects.

entries.title: Under the Hood: weighted top score contributions
entries.summary: Requested Under the Hood traces can now carry the largest weighted score contributions rather than only raw prediction heads.
details: VM Ranker selects up to three terms by absolute contribution, retaining a term only when its absolute share of the sum of absolute contributions is at least 0.10.
Named weighted_terms replace the old scalar-only sum. Cached scoring requests can also produce contributions when explicitly requested.
The trace page requires login, a feature switch and a decodable payload. It returns unavailable/404 when the required path is unavailable.
entries.practical_meaning: If the interface is available, use it as partial evidence about one scoring step, alongside candidate and visibility information.
limits: This is not a full causal explanation of impressions, a list of every recommendation decision, or evidence that all accounts have access.

entries.title: Under the Hood: labeled post lists and conditional appeals
entries.summary: The report code adds labeled-post IDs and conditional appeal information, with backend and UI feature switches; public defaults do not make them universally visible.
details: The data pipeline collects per-label IDs with a storage cap of 500. Serving normally shows up to three; above three it suppresses the list when labeled posts exceed 5% of the monthly cohort, otherwise selects up to 50 recent IDs. Takedown lists bypass that percentage rule.
Backend report-post-ID, appeals and sensitive-media appeal flags default false; the report UI has its own post-ID flag. A visible list can include posts that had a label earlier, even after removal.

Appeal guidance depends on label family and feature flags. For supported post-label appeals, the guidance says the label must still be present; the report does not verify its current state. Account-label appeals are always absent in this report implementation.

Existing cohort rules remain: at least 10 eligible posts, account older than 365 days, the ten-day month-readiness window, and incomplete-data fallback. Reposts/nullcasts remain excluded and edit chains are deduplicated logically. Label categories and described effects did not gain a new penalty just because IDs became reportable.
entries.practical_meaning: When available, save the actual report period and affected posts and inspect the stated label. A missing list or removed label does not prove there was no earlier label.
limits: This is reporting and appeal plumbing, not a new universal punishment or rollout announcement. Existing eligibility and observation limits still apply.

entries.title: New notification filters are not new Home recommendation penalties
entries.summary: Visibility evaluation expands to mention, reply, media-tag, like and repost notifications. Their rules must not be copied into claims about all Home recommendations.
details: Mention/reply notifications add DUPLICATE_CONTENT and SMYTE_SPAM_TWEET drops for non-authors; LOW_QUALITY has an older-post condition (not newer than 2019-04-01).

DUPLICATE_MENTION, ABUSIVE, UNTRUSTED_URL and DOWNRANK_SPAM_REPLY apply to non-followers with the viewer quality filter enabled; RISKY_HIGH_VIZ_REPLY applies to non-followers. Existing SPAM_HIGH_RECALL remains.
Media-tag notification handling uses actor/account and follow-relationship rules with a community exception, not the whole mention/reply post-label list.
Like/repost notifications check the actor and that the referenced post exists and belongs to the recipient; their PureCore post fetch does not hydrate the full safety-label rules.
entries.practical_meaning: If an expected notification is missing, inspect its notification-specific audience and conditions. Do not infer account-wide reach suppression from that alone.
limits: This diff does not add these mention/reply notification rules to the Home recommendation lists.

entries.title: Geographic media restriction and promoted hydration surfaces
entries.summary: GeoRestrictedMedia is added to ordinary TimelineHome with a non-author audience; a separate promoted-hydration surface is also introduced.
details: The geographic media rule audience changes Everyone -> NonAuthors wherever that rule is used. HomeRecommendations already has its DMCA rule.
TimelineHomePromotedHydration is a distinct rule list. Dynamic-product-ad limited-engagement reasons depend on feature/policy evaluation, not a blanket advertising exemption.
EvaluateTweets can distinguish deleted and bounce-deleted results from not-found. Much of the rest is hydration and notice/appeal refactoring; action precedence remains unchanged.
entries.practical_meaning: For a visibility diagnosis, identify the viewer region, author/non-author relation and exact display surface before drawing conclusions.
limits: A different hydration surface does not mean advertisements bypass all moderation.

entries.title: Media tags now count in one mention-based safety task
entries.summary: One realtime safety-task eligibility check now counts unique text mentions together with media-tag handles.
details: The numeric threshold remains two; unique, case-insensitive handle counting across text mentions and media tags is new. Previously this path counted whitespace-delimited words starting with @, including repetitions. High-PageRank/gray-badge exclusions, delay and prior SpamHighRecall checks remain.
Selection for a classifier is not a violation result or an enforcement action. Classifier input can now include media tags.
entries.practical_meaning: Tag people because they are relevant to the post. Do not interpret two tags as an automatic ban, and do not assume media tagging avoids mention-related checks.
limits: This is one task-selection path, not a universal hashtag/mention limit.

entries.title: Safety cache and enforcement plumbing: keep cache time separate from penalties
entries.summary: Safety labels gain optional shared cache support and enforcement-control changes. Cache lifetimes are not label penalty durations.
details: The new Dragonfly cache accepts found results for 24 hours and not-found results for ten minutes as read-freshness limits; physical writes use a 24-hour TTL for both. Shadow/serve rollout buckets default to zero. Existing local ten-second caching remains; stale outage fallback still filters expired labels.
An unknown valid non-factory classifier head with no head/alias control row defaults to Recording rather than Rules. That default records without adding enforcement actions.
PageActionSuspend adds permanent/policy options; the legacy default remains non-permanent PlatformManipulation. Permanent upgrades are distinguished in deduplication.

The video hidden-overlay detector changes threshold -1.75 -> -1.0 and skips its reveal step for sufficiently opaque motion (>0.35), alongside prompt changes. This is detector behavior, not a new creator reward.
entries.practical_meaning: Use the actual label and its applicability to diagnose restrictions. Do not tell creators that a cache setting establishes a 24-hour penalty.
limits: Optional cache rollout, classifier eligibility, enforcement policy and label expiry are different layers.

entries.title: Grok Analyze and Post Video score fields have zero public weights
entries.summary: ReactWithVideo is renamed to PostVideo and GrokAnalyze is added. Both named weights remain zero in Home Mixer and VM Ranker.
details: The value-model structure adds corresponding named predictions/terms. Existence of a field is not evidence of an active bonus.
No separate explicit Article-completion reward is introduced by these fields.
entries.practical_meaning: Do not advise creators to summon Grok or add video merely to collect a supposed new score bonus.
limits: Effective production overrides are unknown; zero public defaults are not proof of every live setting either.

entries.title: Optional retrieval and page-ranking extensions remain unproven creator bonuses
entries.summary: Two-tower retrieval and page reward code add options, without public nonzero/default-enabled evidence for universal use.
details: Two-tower objective blending accepts tweet_click; w_tweet_click defaults to 0 and objective_head_weights is empty.
PageRL adds DM/copy-link reward coefficients defaulting to zero; generic sharing remains 4.
PageDecodeRewardHead is new with default 0; request fields eta, nu_author, nu_sid and prior_tau are left unset by Home Mixer. EnablePageDecodeRerank and EnablePageRlExploration remain false.
Existing page completion_bonus=1 concerns an impressed slate and the final slot video-quality-view condition, not reading an Article to its final word.
entries.practical_meaning: Do not turn an optional retrieval head or page reward into a rule that one share type, Article completion or posting cadence guarantees more exposure.
limits: Training, retrieval, item scoring and whole-page selection are separate stages.

entries.title: Unchanged: daily frequency myth, cold start, Article and first-image boundaries
entries.summary: The compared code still does not impose a daily second-post discount or a universal Article bonus; the relevant author-count, cold-start and V8.2 rendering mechanisms did not change.
details: author_pool_counts and post-fusion behavior remain the same: per-candidate-batch counts, not an accumulating daily count. VM diversity defaults still yield 1, 0.625, 0.4375 with decay 0.5 and floor 0.25.
author_cold_start.rs and fair_share_ranking_filter.rs are byte-identical over the interval. Ordinary AgeFilter retains 48 hours; that is not a universal lifetime for every surface.

renderer_v82.py is byte-identical: a 4000-character text path, a 200-character Article-title path and the first available image/video media path remain. This is not all X models: V8 Search has a different multiple-media budget.
Candidate filtering retains the same main predicates; allocation/partition refactoring does not establish a new posting rule.
entries.practical_meaning: Keep choosing Article, Post or Thread by the material and reader needs. Publish a second useful piece when it is ready; the code supplies no daily second-post timer to wait out.
limits: Rechecked source behavior is not verification of every production configuration, guaranteed exposure or unchanged model weights.

entries.title: Engineering changes and a reverted ads experiment
entries.summary: Not every changed line changes creator-facing behavior: this interval includes observability, storage, inference and test refactors, plus a reverted ads-blending default.
details: AdsBlenderType changes multi_risk -> slot_spread in 9106e9f, then back in b220448; the interval has no net change to that default. Following ad-spacing logic is unchanged, while drop-cause logs and campaign metadata are added.
Ad history gains an XDC cache-write default with a 300-second TTL and injection logging. Those are storage/diagnostic settings, not a publishing interval.
The new candidate-pipeline result_size_for(query) method delegates to the existing result_size() by default, with no repository override found.
Video inference handles cached candidates and missing predictions more explicitly; model-loading and cache fallback changes are operational behavior, not proof of increased video distribution.
entries.practical_meaning: Use the separate upstream changelog to distinguish durable behavior changes from temporary settings and implementation maintenance.
limits: The review compares public code. It does not measure production experiments or account-level effects.
